claim: SIA reports that foundational chip sales volume rose 6.3% in 2025 compared with 2024.
evidence: "Foundational chip sales volume, however, increased modestly at 6.3% in 2025 compared to 2024." (SIA 2026 State of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry, p. 6)

metric.name: foundational chip unit volume growth
metric.population: SIA 'foundational' chips (category not defined in the report)

notes: Corrects CLM-1321 by dropping its 'meaning unit prices fell' inference: SIA's value figure (-5.2%) is measured against the 2022 peak, while the volume figure (+6.3%) is against 2024, so the two cannot be combined into a price change.

claim: After replacing Q2 2026 with actual data, WSTS's recalculated 2026 growth rates (August 2026) were about 25% for micro, 11% for analog, 12% for discretes, 8% for optoelectronics and 2% for sensors, versus Spring 2026 forecasts of 20%, 10%, 8%, 3% and 3%.
evidence: paraphrase: 'Segment Growth Y/Y' table, 2026 column, in Chart 3 of the WSTS Q2 2026 release (read from the chart image): Discretes 12%, Analog 11%, Micro 25%, Optoelectronics 8%, Sensors 2%. Text: "For 2026, calculations for all product segments become slightly higher, except Sensors."

metric.name: micro IC growth, recalculated
metric.methodology: WSTS Spring 2026 forecast with Q2 2026 actuals substituted; Q3 onward uses the June assumptions, not a new forecast

notes: Values were read from a chart image (rounded integers), not a data table. They agree with the release text, which says every segment except sensors was revised up. Newer data relevant to CLM-1317.
